speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe exactly how your cough feels, and does it produce any mucus? If so, what color is the mucus and how much do you cough up? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hyperinflation with flattened diaphragms, increased retrosternal airspace and a prominent hilar shadow suggestive of emphysema.

speaker: Doctor
text: That chest X-ray strongly suggests emphysema; have you been diagnosed with COPD or chronic bronchitis in the past? Additionally, does your shortness of breath worsen significantly during physical activity or cold weather?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I haven't been formally diagnosed with COPD or chronic bronchitis before, though I know I smoke a lot. The shortness of breath definitely gets much worse when I try to walk up stairs or go out in the cold. I don't have a fever or any weight loss, just this constant cough and feeling tight in my chest. However, the stroke team confirmed ischemic stroke before transfer. This session should only record the confirmed diagnosis, not re-assess.
